title: Cock Blocked
summary: Chapter 4 opens with a Korean/Mangchi performance whose repeated phonetic refrain and heavy musical overlap defeat ordinary English ASR. The cleaner correctly collapses most repeated Oh and Oh my gosh runs, but one enormous `cál` decoder loop survives at 163 seconds and must be regenerated rather than published. The studio begins at 3:50 with Steve Lee beatboxing, Bill Poon, Val, Bobby Trivia and Critter Fleming; Money Mark is touring in Copenhagen and Asa Akira is away for a family emergency. A recap of Justene Jaro and Dawn makes the video requirement explicit: the prior wrestling, this episode's onesie/photo poses, and the colored-light post-show physical sequence are not recoverable from audio alone. The first title story concerns Bill's repeated invitations to a group Filipino barbecue. By his account, a third invitation receives no response; the room explicitly names the line between crush and stalking, and Bill says he is done. David's counterclaim—that money, fame or art can move someone beyond the creep zone—remains his rhetoric, not consent. Ignored private texts, screenshots, pickup details and home routes are not republished. Steve joins Bill for the pickup, creating Bill's fear that Steve will cock-block him. The Comedy Store movement follows: Critter is made the object of Bobby Lee crowd work; David later sees Dean Delray, likely Sebastian Maniscalco, Bobby Lee and a surprise Chris Rock set. Chris Rock's quiet reception while testing BET Awards material, followed by stronger Jerrod Carmichael and Esther Povitsky sets, produces a valuable creative-process argument about polished repetition versus experimentation in public. The room's open-mic, pay-to-play and joke-writing discussion is preserved alongside its racial and antisemitic stereotyping, but those generalizations are not facts. A late-night grocery story contrasts impatience and contemptuous descriptions of an unhoused couple with a concrete offer: anything they can collect in ten minutes. They choose food, alcohol, hygiene goods and dog food. David briefly considers filming, then does not; that choice preserves dignity and is more important than converting the people into proof of generosity. The second title story concerns a private woman whom David says he intermittently dated for three years. He presents romance as multiple simultaneous games, states sexual interest, criticizes her phone use and describes consensual breast/genital contact before Critter's announced arrival interrupts them. Critter says he texted his arrival time; David ultimately acknowledges the interruption was not intentional. David then proposes a Mangchi hammer-and-oil photo shoot. The woman cancels for the BET Awards. Prior flirting, nudity, touching, or agreement to a photo concept does not make a later cancellation invalid. David issues an ultimatum, and the private text exchange escalates. Her direct sentence—Please do not text me anymore—is the decisive boundary. He continues with insults and later admits wanting the last word. The archive retains this chronology and the ideas without publishing screenshots, identity clues or a contact trail. The episode then becomes an unusually direct account of failed emotional escape: guilt leads to work, sex with two reportedly painkiller-impaired private participants, money after sex, a food binge, self-induced vomiting and what David calls a manic episode. He says none of it makes him feel better. Masturbation without pornography is proposed as a way not to involve other people; that is part of the conversation, not clinical advice. Trivia later repeats that the third no means no, although one clear no already suffices. The close promotes the historical YouTube channel, sticker app and Mangchi, asks the audience to help Bill's dating prospects, then moves into a highly visual physical-comedy sequence and a closing song. No line-level speaker names publish: this artifact still has zero validated acoustic turns or identity windows.

source_notes: The cleaner records 259 edits: 147 empty artifacts and 112 degenerate-run edits, reducing 2,219 raw segments to 1,999 clean segments.
A large repeated `cál` string survives at 163.5 seconds despite the degenerate-run pass. This is a cleaner defect, not meaningful speech, and blocks publication of that span until regeneration.
Musical performance remains the weakest ASR region. Phonetic Korean and overlapping lyrics must not be silently converted into confident English.

Critter Fleming, Jerrod Carmichael, Esther Povitsky, BET Awards, Mangchi and Rutger Hauer are high-confidence entity repairs; Sebastian Maniscalco and Asa Akira's Insatiable remain marked likely until direct audiovisual confirmation.
The direct YouTube callout and multiple visual-only scenes make full video part of source completeness, not an optional enhancement.
Zero validated acoustic turns/windows means no line-level named speakers publish.
